function: Learned DQN jointly decides task offloading target (local, UAV, satellite) and OFDMA channel allocation on ground-to-air and ground-to-space uplinks to minimize delay-energy cost (p. 9).
system: 3 satellites, 4 UAVs, 20-60 ground devices; OFDMA uplinks, G2A 30-60 MHz and G2S 10-40 MHz; antennas and carrier frequency not stated; no RIS (pp. 11-12).
method: DQN (TOCA-DQN), four-layer network with 256 and 512 hidden neurons, reinforcement learning with replay buffer and target network; CPU allocation by non-learned Newton interior point (pp. 9-11).
data_channel: Custom simulator: deterministic inverse-square channel gain alpha/d^2 (alpha = beta = 1e-5), AWGN, random device, UAV and satellite positions; no fading model or dataset (pp. 3, 11-12).
test_conditions: One simulator for training and evaluation; sweeps of device count (20-60), task size, CPU cycles and bandwidth; reuse of a trained DQN across sweeps is not stated (pp. 11-13).
baselines: Non-learned: genetic algorithm (TOCA-GA), simulated annealing (TOCA-SA), random (TOCA-RA); no earlier learned method (p. 12).
metrics: Total system cost (weighted delay and energy), cumulative reward versus iterations, percentage cost reduction against baselines (pp. 12-13).
q1_support: p. 3: "When user device n offloads a task to UAV u, the channel gain gn,u can be expressed as" an inverse-square distance gain alpha/d^2 (Table II, p. 12: alpha, beta = 1e-5); custom simulator, with no 3GPP TR 38.811, DeepMIMO or measured data mentioned.
q2_support: p. 12: "Fig. 5 illustrates the variation in the total system cost for all four algorithms as the number of user devices changes from 20 to 60" is a sweep of the environment; the paper never states that a trained DQN is tested in an unseen setting or adapted.
q3_support: p. 12: "comparing the performance of the TOCA-DQN algorithm with the task offloading and channel allocation genetic algorithm", plus TOCA-SA (simulated annealing) and TOCA-RA (random); only non-learned baselines, no earlier learned method or other DRL algorithm is compared.
q4_support: p. 11: "the two hidden layers having 256 and 512 neurons, respectively" gives only the architecture; no complexity order, FLOPs, parameter count or runtime is reported (Theorems 1-6, pp. 7-11, concern optimality and convergence of the interior-point steps).
q5_support: p. 11: "the ground user devices are randomly distributed within a 200-m by 200-m square" describes the paper's own simulated scenario; no code or data link, public dataset or measured data is mentioned.
notes: Borderline above_phy, included. p. 9: the DQN action a_t = {a_n^p, b_s^q, eps_n,u, eta_n,s} joins task offloading (above PHY) with OFDMA channel allocation on G2A and G2S links (resource allocation on aerial and satellite links, physical layer by the protocol), so area 6; a reviewer who reads the channel choice as user association or scheduling should exclude it as above_phy. UAV and satellite CPU allocation is solved by non-learned Newton interior point (pp. 6-8). Section III says geosynchronous satellites (p. 3) but Section VII uses low Earth orbit satellites at 100-500 km (p. 11). Table II cites [33] and [34] for alpha, beta and the noise powers, absent from the 32-entry reference list. Tables I and II read from page images (pp. 3, 12).
